deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a (finite) arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane, seen as a 1-complex K^1 (vertices are intersection points, edges are segments of pseudolines). For each pseudoline D, Ω(D) is a 2-element set, almost certainly the two orientations (directions of travel) of D. The aim, as the next page makes explicit, is to rebuild from the combinatorics alone the orientation local system of the plane on the 1-skeleton.

Top of page (end of a case analysis from the previous page): in the residual case one gets the complete configuration of 6 pseudolines joining in pairs the four vertices u, u', v, t (a complete quadrangle). There one checks directly that the bijection φ_s : Ω(D) ≅ Ω(D') defined by s equals the one defined by a point v lying in the same one of the two regions of X cut out by D and D'.

Main part (axiomatisation). K^1 is a 1-complex subdivided into pseudolines, such that every vertex lies on at least 2 pseudolines and two distinct pseudolines meet in exactly one point. For distinct D, D' and a vertex s on neither, one wants a bijection φ_{s;D,D'} : Ω(D) ≅ Ω(D'). Classically this is 'perspectivity from s': transport the orientation of D to D' through the pencil of pseudolines at s. The required properties are:
(a) On the set of pseudolines not through s, the system (φ_{s;D,D'}) is 'simply transitive', i.e. it satisfies the cocycle condition φ_{D',D''}∘φ_{D,D'} = φ_{D,D''} and φ_{D,D} = id.
(b) Let Δ be a third pseudoline meeting D and D' at x and x' (x = x' allowed). For s, s' on Δ distinct from x and x', φ_{s;D,D'} = φ_{s';D,D'} iff s and s' lie on the same one of the two arcs into which x and x' cut Δ. So φ_{a;D,D'} and φ_{a';D,D'} are defined for the two arcs a and a'. Crossing D or D' along Δ flips the identification, as it does for real perspectivities.
(c) (unfinished on this page) Let t = D∩D', and let Δ_1, Δ_2 be two pseudolines through s but not through t, meeting D at u_i and D' at u'_i. This presumably sets up a comparison of φ_s with the maps induced by the segments u_i u'_i.

Next page: when there is no monogon or bigon (i.e. the arrangement is not a pencil or a double pencil), define Ω(s) as the quotient (colimit) of the Ω(D), D not through s, under the φ_s. Ω(s) is a 2-element set, in effect the local orientation of the plane at s, i.e. the sense of rotation of the pencil at s. Then make s ↦ Ω(s) a local system on K^1 using (b). Its monodromy around a pseudoline should be nontrivial, recovering the non-orientability (w_1) of RP^2.

The problem served is a purely combinatorial or axiomatic reconstruction of the topology (orientation sheaf, hence the 2-cells and the surface) of a pseudoline arrangement from its incidence 1-complex, in the spirit of tame/combinatorial topology.
errors: Property (a) as written ('simplement transitif') is ambiguous. What is meant is the transitivity/cocycle compatibility of the system φ_s on the pseudolines not through s; uniqueness of the transition maps is automatic since they are given.

In (b) the case x = x' (Δ through t = D∩D') is explicitly allowed. Then the 'two arcs' degenerate: the complement of one point in a circle is a single arc. So all s on Δ give the same φ, and the statement needs that reading.

The axioms on K^1 (each vertex on ≥2 pseudolines, two pseudolines meet in exactly one point) are those of an abstract linear space. They do not by themselves guarantee existence of the φ's; finite projective planes satisfy them combinatorially. The page postulates the φ's with properties rather than constructing them, and the previous pages construct them case by case.
Uniqueness fails in the pencil and double-pencil cases (monogons/bigons), as the next page acknowledges. This is not an error but a necessary exclusion.

ideas.what: Bijection between orientation sets of two pseudolines induced by a point off both (perspectivity), with sign flip when the centre crosses D or D' along a third line
ideas.modern_name: Perspectivity / orientation transport; sign behaviour of the chirotope of a rank-3 oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical projective geometry; for pseudolines Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Folkman–Lawrence (1978), Goodman–Pollack

ideas.what: Defining Ω(s) as the colimit of Ω(D) over pseudolines avoiding s, and assembling the Ω(s) into a local system of 2-element sets on the 1-skeleton
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial orientation double cover / orientation local system (w_1) of RP^2 on an arrangement graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in oriented matroid theory and topological representation theorems (Folkman–Lawrence)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to tame-topology and combinatorial themes; no explicit treatment of pseudolines known to me

ideas.what: Axiomatic setup: a 1-complex subdivided into pseudolines with any two meeting in exactly one point, plus a system of perspectivity bijections satisfying (a), (b), (c)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial characterization of pseudoline arrangement graphs / topological projective planes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grünbaum (Arrangements and Spreads, 1972); Goodman–Pollack; Bokowski et al.

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic route from the incidence 1-complex of a pseudoline arrangement to the orientation local system of the projective plane, via a coherent system of perspectivities. He excludes exactly the pencil/double-pencil cases. Property (c) is left unfinished on this page.
missed.quote: on a une bijection φ_{s;D,D'} Ω(D) ≃ Ω(D') avec les propriétés suivantes : a) ... b) ... c) Soit t l'intersection de D et D'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a sheaf-theoretic or local-system phrasing of orientation data that oriented matroid theory normally encodes by chirotopes. It is mildly interesting historically as Grothendieck's own route. It is unlikely to contain results unknown to specialists, given Folkman–Lawrence and the extensive literature on arrangements.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, characteristic Grothendieck reformulation (colimits of 2-element sets, a local system on the 1-skeleton) of orientation data for pseudoline arrangements. The underlying mathematics (perspectivities, the orientation of RP^2, combinatorial characterisation of arrangements) is well covered by oriented matroid theory. The historical interest lies in his engagement with the topic, not in new results.
transcription_corrections: 'qui est dans le = des deux régions' should read 'qui est dans la même des deux régions'; the '=' sign is Grothendieck's abbreviation for 'même'. Likewise 'appartiennent au = des deux arcs' means 'appartiennent au même des deux arcs'.
'défini par v_1' is probably 'défini par v' (the fourth vertex u, u', v, t), possibly with a subscript.
In (a), 'Sur l'une des ps. droites ... l'ensemble des φ' should read 'Sur l'ens. des ps. droites (D, D', ...) qui ne passent pas par s, le syst. des φ_{s;D,D'} est simplement transitif'.
The insertion under K^1 reads roughly '(tout sommet appartenant à au moins 2 ps. dr., et 2 ps. droites se rencontrant en un pt et un seul)'.
'Soit t l'élément intersection' is more likely 'Soit t le pt d'intersection de D et D''.
'leurs int. avec D (D')' means 'leurs intersections avec D (resp. D')'.
